p.i: nibus approbari existimo. Nam bruta animantia juxta ac homines sensibus tum externis, tum internis, si physicae scientiae peritis fidem adhibeamus, præditi sunt. Si igitur homines, initio non ad obscuram aliquam effigiem creati, effecti, formati: sed ad divinam imaginem à Deo Opt. Max. conditi, fa-cti, fabricati: per lapsum autem nostrorum primorum parentum in extremas ignorantiarum tenebras conjecti, & præcipitati: nullis artium liberalium axiomatibus imbuantur, instituantur, ac erudiantur: plane inter bruta animantia sunt numerandi. Deus autem I E H O V A humanum genus ab istiusmodi mentis tenebris vindicaturus, pro sua immensa misericordia ac bonitate⁓ Patriarchas, & reliquos Vates insigni ac eximia intelligentia, sapientia ac eruditione⁓ ornavit, ut cæteros[?], ingenuas non callentes scientias, divina sapientia erudirent. Sic Jo-sephus Genef.41. prædicatur à Pharaone omnium Sapientum sapientissimus, hisce verbis: Nunquid sapientiorem & consimilem tui invenire potero? Sic 3.lib. Regum cap.4. page.notes: The tetragrammaton is printed as spaced capitals I E H O V A, with a final V-like glyph that is not clearly legible; copied as IEHOVA. The sign after "bonitate" and "eruditione" is a flourish, read as an abbreviation mark (⁓) and not certain. "cæteros" is set with a ligature-like initial; marked [?]. No margin notes, page number or signature visible. Lower right "dentiam" is treated as catchword.
